- Debug/explain output exposing component score contributions
- Tests validating stable ordering under representative queries

## Why this matters
Explainable, deterministic fusion is required for operator trust and practical debugging.

## Acceptance
- Hybrid ranking improves agreed quality metrics over lexical baseline
- Fallback behavior prevents semantic outages from breaking search
- Score diagnostics allow rapid triage of ranking anomalies

title: Enforce semantic latency/cost budgets with caching and adaptive controls
description:
## Context
Embedding generation and vector retrieval introduce cost and latency risks. Budgets/caching are required for sustainable always-on operation.

## Scope
Define and implement latency/cost budget controls (batching, caching, adaptive refresh) for semantic path.

## Deliverables
- Budget targets and guardrails (p95 latency, per-day compute cost)
- Cache design for embeddings/query results with invalidation policy
- Rate-limit/backpressure behavior for embedding pipeline
- Telemetry dashboards for cost/latency tracking

## Why this matters
A high-quality semantic system that is too slow or expensive cannot be kept enabled in production.

## Acceptance
- Semantic path stays within defined cost/latency envelopes under representative load
- Cache invalidation is correct and tested
- Operators can monitor budget consumption in near real time

title: [replay] Epic: Deterministic Swarm Replay + Counterfactual Simulator
description:
Build a deterministic replay and counterfactual simulation capability for FrankenTerm that can take a real swarm run (captured deltas/events/detections/policy decisions/workflow actions), replay it offline, and compare baseline vs candidate behavior with auditable decision diffs.\n\nThis is intended to convert incidents and real operational traces into reproducible regression artifacts and pre-deploy safety gates.

## Success Criteria
1. The complete epic scope is delivered across child beads with no unresolved critical blockers and no loss of declared capability.
2. Every child feature/task in this epic includes comprehensive unit tests plus deterministic integration/E2E scenarios.
3. The epic includes an end-to-end validation matrix covering happy paths, failure injection, recovery behavior, and sustained/soak execution where applicable.
4. Structured logging and artifact standards are enforced across epic deliverables (timestamp, correlation_id, scenario_id, decision path, reason_code/error_code) with triage-ready evidence bundles.
5. Verification demonstrates stable, repeatable outcomes across reruns and confirms policy/safety invariants for all touched subsystems.

## User Impact
1. Specify the concrete operator/agent workflow pain this bead removes (speed, reliability, safety, or clarity).
2. Define measurable user-facing outcomes (for example p95 latency, failure/timeout rate, time-to-recovery, or reduction in manual intervention steps).
3. Define no-regression UX guarantees and explicit rollback/degradation behavior if those outcomes are not met.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Can capture complete replay artifacts from real runs into a stable .ftreplay format.
2. Can replay baseline deterministically with no external side effects.
3. Can replay with counterfactual overrides (rules, policy, workflow variants).
4. Produces structured diff reports showing decision and effect drift with severity.
5. Integrates with CI and supports go or no-go quality gates before rollout.
6. Includes operator docs, rollback-safe rollout strategy, and incident-response playbooks.
7. Includes comprehensive unit, property, integration, and e2e coverage for capture, replay, diff, and interfaces.
8. Includes structured JSON logging and traceability standards for every e2e harness and CI gate run.
notes: Strategic intent: make ft behavior provable before production rollout.\nWhy now: project complexity and concurrent swarm work makes regressions likely; this provides a durable safety+velocity multiplier.\nNon-goal: perfect simulation of every external system at v1; start with deterministic core and explicit unsupported domains.

comments.author: Jeff Emanuel
comments.text: Program rationale: this capability is the bridge between observability and safe automation. It makes incidents replayable, turns manual debugging into deterministic evaluation, and creates a compounding artifact library for future quality gates. This epic is intentionally split into tracks that can run in parallel once upstream contracts are fixed.

title: [replay][T1.3] Capture policy/workflow decision and action provenance
description:
Record policy evaluations, workflow trigger decisions, action intents, and final outcomes as first-class replay entities so decision diffs can explain behavioral drift, not just output drift.

## Deliverables

### DecisionCaptureAdapter
- `DecisionCaptureAdapter` struct wraps pattern engine + workflow engine + policy engine
- Intercepts `Detection`, `StepResult`, `PolicyDecision` at decision boundary
- Emits `DecisionEvent` with: decision_type, input_hash, output, rule_id, definition_hash, confidence, timestamp_ms, pane_id, causality chain
- `definition_hash`: FNV-1a of the rule/workflow/policy definition text — enables counterfactual root-cause attribution
- `input_hash`: SHA-256 of the input that triggered the decision — enables deterministic replay verification

### DecisionEvent Schema
- `decision_type`: enum { PatternMatch, WorkflowStep, PolicyEvaluation }
- `rule_id`: String — which rule/step/policy produced this decision
- `definition_hash`: u64 — FNV-1a hash of rule definition source
- `input_summary`: truncated UTF-8 of matched text (max 256 bytes, redaction-safe)
- `output`: serde_json::Value — the Detection/StepResult/PolicyDecision serialized
- `parent_event_id`: links back to the RecorderEvent that triggered this decision
- `confidence`: Option<f64> for pattern detections

### Integration Points
- Hook into patterns.rs PatternEngine::evaluate() exit path
- Hook into workflows.rs WorkflowRunner::step() return path
- Hook into policy.rs PolicyEngine::evaluate() return path
- Each hook is zero-cost when capture is disabled (feature-gated behind replay-capture)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- DecisionEvent serialization roundtrip
- definition_hash stability across identical rule text
- definition_hash changes when rule text changes
- input_hash determinism for same input
- input_summary truncation at 256 bytes
- input_summary redaction strips sensitive patterns
- PatternMatch capture from Detection
- WorkflowStep capture from StepResult::Continue/Done/Retry/Abort
- PolicyEvaluation capture from Allow/Deny/Elevate
- Causality chain parent_event_id linkage
- Feature gate: no capture when replay-capture disabled
- Empty/missing fields handled gracefully

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_decision_capture.sh
- Scenario 1: Run pattern engine against known text, verify DecisionEvent emitted with correct rule_id and definition_hash
- Scenario 2: Run workflow step, verify StepResult captured with parent linkage
- Scenario 3: Run policy evaluation, verify Allow/Deny decision captured
- Scenario 4: Disable replay-capture feature, verify zero DecisionEvents emitted
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"decision_capture","scenario":N,"event_count":N,"definition_hashes":[...],"status":"pass|fail","duration_ms":N}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Without decision provenance, operators see that behavior diverged but not why. This bead makes every divergence explainable.
- Measurable outcome: 100% of decision-diff divergences include rule_id + definition_hash for root-cause attribution.
- No-regression: Existing pattern/workflow/policy behavior unchanged; capture is additive and feature-gated.

5. Release/promotion decisions are gated by auditable evidence bundles and explicit go/no-go criteria.

title: [replay][T1.4] Enforce redaction, sensitivity classification, and retention boundaries
description:
Apply redaction and sensitivity policies during artifact capture so replay bundles preserve determinism-relevant semantics without leaking secrets or violating retention constraints.

## Deliverables

### CaptureRedactor
- CaptureRedactor struct with configurable redaction rules
- Operates on RecorderEvent stream between capture and serialization
- Sensitivity tiers: T1 (standard, safe for CI), T2 (internal, team access), T3 (restricted, incident-only)
- Redaction modes: mask (replace with block chars), hash (one-way SHA-256), drop (remove field entirely)
- Token patterns: API keys (sk-*, AKIA*, ghp_*, xoxb-*), JWT tokens, connection strings, bearer tokens
- Custom patterns via redaction_rules.toml config file

### SensitivityClassifier
- Classifies each RecorderEvent field into sensitivity tier
- IngressText.content: scan for token patterns, T2/T3 if found, else T1
- EgressOutput.content: same scanning
- Detection.matched_text: inherit tier from source event
- PolicyDecision.context: always T2 minimum (may contain internal details)
- Classifier is deterministic: same input always gets same classification

### RetentionEnforcer
- Enforces per-tier retention limits at artifact write time
- T1: 90 days default, T2: 30 days, T3: 7 days (all configurable)
- Expired artifacts are tombstoned (header preserved, content replaced with REDACTED_EXPIRED)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Each token pattern correctly detected
- Mask mode replaces with correct-length replacement string
- Hash mode produces deterministic SHA-256 replacement
- Drop mode removes field entirely, preserving event structure
- T1/T2/T3 classification for each RecorderEventPayload variant
- Sensitivity inheritance for Detection events
- Mixed-tier event: highest tier wins
- Redaction is idempotent
- Redacted events still pass schema validation
- Custom patterns from redaction_rules.toml loaded correctly
- Retention enforcer tombstones expired T3 artifacts
- Unicode content redaction preserves valid UTF-8 boundaries

### Proptest Properties (P-06 through P-08 from taxonomy)
- Redaction stability: redacting same event twice yields identical output
- Redacted events still deserialize and pass schema validation
- No original secret text appears in redacted output

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_redaction.sh
- Scenario 1: Capture with known API key in pane output, verify masked in .ftreplay
- Scenario 2: Set sensitivity to T1, verify T2/T3 fields dropped
- Scenario 3: Set retention to 0 days for T3, verify tombstoning
- Scenario 4: Roundtrip redacted artifact, verify no data loss in non-redacted fields
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"redaction","scenario":N,"secrets_found":N,"secrets_redacted":N,"tier":"T1|T2|T3","status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Operators cannot safely share replay artifacts because they may contain secrets. This bead makes artifacts safe-by-default.
- Measurable outcome: Zero secret leaks in T1 artifacts (verified by automated secret scanning in CI).
- No-regression: Existing recorder_audit.rs A0-A4 tiers unchanged; capture redaction is an additional layer.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Scope is fully preserved with no feature/behavior regression relative to the parent contract.
2. Comprehensive unit tests cover happy paths, boundary/edge cases, and explicit failure/error branches.
3. Deterministic integration and end-to-end scripts validate nominal, degraded, failure, and recovery scenarios.
4. Validation emits structured logs/artifacts with at least: `timestamp`, `component`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `decision_path`, `inputs`, `outcome`, `reason_code`/`error_code`, and `artifact_path`.
5. Release/promotion decisions are gated by auditable evidence bundles and explicit go/no-go criteria.

title: [replay][T1.5] Add artifact chunking, compression, hashing, and integrity validation
description:
Implement the complete .ftreplay v1 artifact writer and packaging pipeline.

## Writer Implementation (core deliverable)
Assemble captured RecorderEvent records, entity metadata, and decision records into the 5-section .ftreplay format per docs/replay-ftreplay-schema-v1.md:
- Section marker emission (--- ftreplay-header/entities/timeline/decisions/footer ---)
- Header generation with capture metadata, content counts, sensitivity tier, integrity checksums
- Entity section: pane and session entities from capture context
- Timeline section: events in strict RecorderMergeKey order, one JSONL line per event
- Decisions section: detection/workflow/policy decisions with definition hashes
- Footer generation with verification metadata and invariant report
- SHA-256 integrity checksums computed per-section and embedded in header

## Chunking (for traces >100K events)
- Chunk boundary logic with configurable chunk size
- Per-chunk .ftreplay files, each independently valid
- Manifest file (trace.manifest.json) with chunk ordering and cross-chunk causality references

## Compression
- gzip and zstd support with auto-detection on read via file magic bytes
- Extensions: .ftreplay.gz, .ftreplay.zst
- Compression applied to entire file, not per-section

## Integrity Validation
- SHA-256 checksum verification on read (compare header checksums against computed values)
- Event count, decision count, entity count validation against header
- Merge order spot-check (first/middle/last) or full verify

## Deliverables
- FtreplayWriter struct with streaming write API (add_entity, add_event, add_decision, finalize)
- FtreplayValidator for read-time integrity checking
- Comprehensive unit tests (>=30) covering writer roundtrip, chunking edge cases, compression roundtrip, integrity violation detection

title: [replay][T1.6] Implement artifact reader, schema migrator, and compatibility checks
description:
Build artifact loader with schema-version compatibility checks and migration hooks so old captures remain usable as format evolves without corrupting deterministic semantics.

## Deliverables

### ArtifactReader
- ArtifactReader::open(path) -> Result<ReplayArtifact> validates magic bytes, parses header, checks schema version
- Supports: raw .ftreplay, gzip .ftreplay.gz, zstd .ftreplay.zst
- Streaming mode: ArtifactReader::stream_events(path) -> impl Iterator<Item=Result<RecorderEvent>> for large artifacts
- Validates footer checksums against computed SHA-256 of timeline + decisions
- Returns ArtifactError::IntegrityMismatch if checksums fail

### SchemaMigrator
- Registry of Migration trait objects: fn migrate(event: Value) -> Result<Value>
- Version chain: v1->v2, v2->v3, etc., migrations compose automatically
- Each migration is a pure function (no side effects)
- migrate_artifact(artifact, target_version) -> Result<MigrationReport>
- MigrationReport: events_migrated, fields_added, fields_removed, warnings

### CompatibilityChecker
- check(artifact_version, engine_version) -> Compatibility enum
- Compatibility: Exact, MigrationAvailable(chain), Incompatible(reason)
- Pre-flight check before replay: Incompatible refuses with clear error
- MigrationAvailable migrates in-memory (original file untouched)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Open valid v1 artifact, parse all sections
- Open gzip and zstd compressed artifacts
- Reject wrong magic bytes, truncated header, mismatched checksums
- Stream 10K-event artifact without loading all into memory
- Schema v1->v2 migration adds new field with default, preserves existing
- Migration chain v1->v3 composes correctly
- Migration is idempotent
- CompatibilityChecker returns correct Compatibility variants
- Error messages include file path and version info
- Empty timeline/decisions sections parse without error

### Proptest Properties (P-14, P-15 from taxonomy)
- Any valid artifact written can be read back with identical event sequence
- Migration chain produces valid schema-conformant output

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_artifact_reader.sh
- Scenario 1: Write then read artifact, verify identical events
- Scenario 2: Corrupt 1 byte in timeline, verify IntegrityMismatch
- Scenario 3: Create v1 artifact, migrate to v2, verify parseable
- Scenario 4: Read artifact with unknown future version, verify Incompatible error
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"artifact_reader","scenario":N,"events_read":N,"version":"v1","compression":"none|gzip|zstd","integrity":"pass|fail","status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: As .ftreplay format evolves, old regression artifacts become unreadable. This bead ensures backward compatibility.
- Measurable outcome: All v1 artifacts remain readable after any future schema evolution.
- No-regression: Existing WAR playback (replay.rs) unchanged; new reader for .ftreplay format.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Scope is fully preserved with no feature/behavior regression relative to the parent contract.
2. Comprehensive unit tests cover happy paths, boundary/edge cases, and explicit failure/error branches.
3. Deterministic integration and end-to-end scripts validate nominal, degraded, failure, and recovery scenarios.
4. Validation emits structured logs/artifacts with at least: `timestamp`, `component`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `decision_path`, `inputs`, `outcome`, `reason_code`/`error_code`, and `artifact_path`.
5. Release/promotion decisions are gated by auditable evidence bundles and explicit go/no-go criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reader validates and reports schema version compatibility.
2. Migration path exists for at least N-1 artifact versions.
3. Migration preserves deterministic meaning (tested).
4. Compatibility failures provide clear remediation guidance.
5. Verification requirement: includes task-scoped unit, integration, and property tests where applicable, at least one end-to-end harness script, and structured JSON logging with deterministic run_id, step, status, duration, and error context fields.
6. e2e harness requirement: at least one realistic e2e script per task path must run in CI and emit structured JSON logs with run_id, scenario_id where relevant, timing, assertions, and failure context.
notes: Replay systems accrue value over time only if old artifacts remain valid.

title: [replay][T2.1] Implement virtual clock and deterministic scheduler core
description:
Implement the virtual clock and deterministic scheduler core for the replay kernel.

## Virtual Clock
- VirtualClock struct that replaces wall-clock time with trace-driven time
- Time advances ONLY when the replay scheduler processes the next event
- Speed control: 1x (wall-clock), 2x (double speed), instant (no delays)
- Clock provides occurred_at_ms and recorded_at_ms for the current event

## Deterministic Scheduler
- ReplayScheduler consumes events from the .ftreplay timeline section
- Events are processed in strict RecorderMergeKey order (5-key total order)
- For each event, the scheduler feeds it to the appropriate engine (pattern, workflow, policy)
- Side effects are isolated (no real I/O, no real pane mutations)
- Scheduler state is serializable for checkpoint/resume support

## Key Invariant
Two runs of the same trace with the same code produce byte-identical decision sequences (EQ-06, EQ-07 from equivalence contract).

## Deliverables
- VirtualClock with speed control API
- ReplayScheduler with event-driven processing loop
- ReplayConfig struct (speed, filters, equivalence level)
- Comprehensive unit tests (>=30): clock advancement, speed modes, ordering verification, determinism proof (replay same trace twice, compare)
- e2e test script: tests/e2e/test_replay_kernel_determinism.sh that captures a trace, replays it twice, and verifies byte-identical decision output

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Deliver full scope for this bead without regressions in adjacent behavior.
2. Add comprehensive unit tests for happy path, boundary/edge behavior, and explicit failure/error handling.
3. Add deterministic integration/end-to-end scenarios including at least one failure injection and one recovery path.
4. Emit detailed structured logs (timestamp, component, correlation_id, scenario_id, inputs, decisions, outcomes, reason_code/error_code) and persist triage artifacts.
5. Document run commands and evidence locations and wire them into normal validation/CI paths.

## User Impact
1. Specify the concrete operator/agent workflow pain this bead removes (speed, reliability, safety, or clarity).
2. Define measurable user-facing outcomes (for example p95 latency, failure/timeout rate, time-to-recovery, or reduction in manual intervention steps).
3. Define no-regression UX guarantees and explicit rollback/degradation behavior if those outcomes are not met.

title: [replay][T2.2] Build stable event ordering and pane merge resolver
description:
Build the stable event ordering and pane merge resolver for multi-pane replay.

## Event Ordering
- Implement RecorderMergeKey-based total ordering for multi-pane event streams
- Merge resolver accepts N pane streams and produces a single ordered output stream
- Verify ordering satisfies EQ-07 (identical merge key ordering between runs)
- Handle concurrent events (same recorded_at_ms) via deterministic tiebreaking

## Pane Merge Resolver
- PaneMergeResolver maintains per-pane iterators over timeline entries
- Produces events in globally sorted order using a priority queue keyed by RecorderMergeKey
- Handles gap markers as first-class events (no skipping)
- Detects and marks clock anomalies per the ClockAnomalyTracker contract

## Deliverables
- PaneMergeResolver with streaming merge API
- Clock anomaly detection and marking during merge
- Comprehensive unit tests (>=30): single-pane ordering, multi-pane merge, concurrent event tiebreaking, gap marker ordering, clock anomaly detection
- Proptest: merge output is always sorted regardless of input pane order (P-10)
- e2e test script: tests/e2e/test_replay_merge_ordering.sh verifying multi-pane traces produce identical ordering across runs

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Deliver full scope for this bead without regressions in adjacent behavior.
2. Add comprehensive unit tests for happy path, boundary/edge behavior, and explicit failure/error handling.
3. Add deterministic integration/end-to-end scenarios including at least one failure injection and one recovery path.
4. Emit detailed structured logs (timestamp, component, correlation_id, scenario_id, inputs, decisions, outcomes, reason_code/error_code) and persist triage artifacts.
5. Document run commands and evidence locations and wire them into normal validation/CI paths.

## User Impact
1. Specify the concrete operator/agent workflow pain this bead removes (speed, reliability, safety, or clarity).
2. Define measurable user-facing outcomes (for example p95 latency, failure/timeout rate, time-to-recovery, or reduction in manual intervention steps).
3. Define no-regression UX guarantees and explicit rollback/degradation behavior if those outcomes are not met.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Canonical ordering rules documented and implemented.
2. Tie-breakers are deterministic and test-covered.
3. Merge behavior for concurrent events is stable across runs.
4. Ordering anomalies produce explicit diagnostics.
5. Verification requirement: includes task-scoped unit, integration, and property tests where applicable, at least one end-to-end harness script, and structured JSON logging with deterministic run_id, step, status, duration, and error context fields.

title: [replay][T2.3] Implement side-effect isolation adapters for replay runtime
description:
Implement side-effect isolation so the replay kernel can execute pattern/workflow/policy logic without triggering real actions (sending keystrokes, spawning processes, calling APIs).

## Deliverables

### SideEffectBarrier
- SideEffectBarrier trait with methods: send_keys, spawn_process, api_call, file_write, emit_notification
- LiveBarrier: passes through to real implementations (production mode)
- ReplayBarrier: captures all side-effect calls into a SideEffectLog, executes nothing
- CounterfactualBarrier: extends ReplayBarrier with override injection points

### SideEffectLog
- Records every intercepted side-effect call with: timestamp_ms, effect_type, target, payload_summary, caller_stack_hint
- Queryable: log.effects_of_type(EffectType::SendKeys), log.effects_for_pane(pane_id)
- Serializable to JSON for inclusion in decision-diff reports

### Adapter Wiring
- PatternEngine receives &dyn SideEffectBarrier — all action triggers go through barrier
- WorkflowRunner receives &dyn SideEffectBarrier — step actions (send_keys, spawn) go through barrier
- PolicyEngine receives &dyn SideEffectBarrier — elevation/notification actions go through barrier
- Existing production code paths unchanged (LiveBarrier is default)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- ReplayBarrier captures send_keys call with correct payload
- ReplayBarrier captures spawn_process with correct args
- ReplayBarrier captures api_call with correct endpoint
- LiveBarrier passes through to real implementation (mock underlying)
- SideEffectLog records in chronological order
- SideEffectLog query by effect_type returns correct subset
- SideEffectLog query by pane_id returns correct subset
- SideEffectLog serialization roundtrip
- CounterfactualBarrier injects override for specific effect
- CounterfactualBarrier passes non-overridden effects to base barrier
- Multiple barriers compose (CounterfactualBarrier wraps ReplayBarrier)
- Barrier is Send+Sync for async compatibility
- Empty SideEffectLog serializes to empty array

### Proptest Properties
- P-09 (from taxonomy): Side-effect isolation completeness — no real effects escape ReplayBarrier under any input sequence

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_side_effect_isolation.sh
- Scenario 1: Replay trace with workflow that triggers send_keys, verify no actual keystrokes sent, SideEffectLog contains entry
- Scenario 2: Replay with policy Elevate decision, verify no notification sent
- Scenario 3: CounterfactualBarrier overrides one send_keys target, verify override recorded
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"side_effect_isolation","scenario":N,"effects_captured":N,"effects_leaked":0,"status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Without isolation, replay would be dangerous — it could send real keystrokes to real panes or trigger real API calls. This bead makes replay safe.
- Measurable outcome: Zero side-effect leaks during replay (verified by SideEffectLog completeness check).
- No-regression: Production code paths unchanged; barrier defaults to LiveBarrier.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Scope is fully preserved with no feature/behavior regression relative to the parent contract.
2. Comprehensive unit tests cover happy paths, boundary/edge cases, and explicit failure/error branches.
3. Deterministic integration and end-to-end scripts validate nominal, degraded, failure, and recovery scenarios.
4. Validation emits structured logs/artifacts with at least: `timestamp`, `component`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `decision_path`, `inputs`, `outcome`, `reason_code`/`error_code`, and `artifact_path`.
5. Release/promotion decisions are gated by auditable evidence bundles and explicit go/no-go criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Replay path cannot trigger live mutating actions.
2. Adapter stubs preserve enough semantics for policy/workflow evaluation.
3. Unsupported side-effect domains fail closed with clear errors.
4. Safety tests prove side-effect isolation.
5. Verification requirement: includes task-scoped unit, integration, and property tests where applicable, at least one end-to-end harness script, and structured JSON logging with deterministic run_id, step, status, duration, and error context fields.
6. e2e harness requirement: at least one realistic e2e script per task path must run in CI and emit structured JSON logs with run_id, scenario_id where relevant, timing, assertions, and failure context.

title: [replay][T2.4] Emit replay provenance logs and decision-explanation trace
description:
Emit structured provenance logs during replay execution so every decision can be traced to its triggering event, input data, and rule version.

## Deliverables

### ReplayProvenanceEmitter
- Emits structured log events at each replay decision point
- Fields: replay_run_id, event_position, event_id, decision_type, rule_id, definition_hash, input_hash, output_summary, wall_clock_ms, virtual_clock_ms
- Log format: JSON lines to configurable sink (file, stdout, buffer)
- Configurable verbosity: minimal (decisions only), standard (decisions + inputs), verbose (decisions + inputs + full event context)

### DecisionExplanationTrace
- For each decision, builds explanation chain: triggering_event -> rule_match -> decision_output
- Includes definition_hash of the rule at replay time vs definition_hash in the artifact (enables counterfactual detection)
- Explanation trace is attached to decision-diff entries as evidence

### Replay Audit Trail
- Append-only log of all replay invocations: who, when, which artifact, which overrides
- Compatible with existing recorder_audit.rs hash-chain format
- Supports verification: tamper-evident chain linking replay runs

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- ProvenanceEmitter emits correct fields for PatternMatch decision
- ProvenanceEmitter emits correct fields for WorkflowStep decision
- ProvenanceEmitter emits correct fields for PolicyEvaluation decision
- replay_run_id is unique per replay invocation
- event_position increments monotonically
- Minimal verbosity omits input data
- Verbose verbosity includes full event context
- DecisionExplanationTrace links triggering_event correctly
- DecisionExplanationTrace detects definition_hash mismatch (counterfactual)
- Audit trail hash chain validates
- Audit trail tamper detection works (modify one entry, chain breaks)

## User Impact
- Pain removed: When replay produces unexpected results, operators need to trace why. Provenance logs provide complete decision archaeology without re-running.

title: [replay][T2.5] Add replay checkpoint/resume and deterministic failure semantics
description:
Add checkpoint/resume capability and deterministic failure semantics so long replay runs can recover from crashes and failures are reproducible.

## Deliverables

### ReplayCheckpointer
- Saves replay state at configurable intervals (default: every 10K events or 60 seconds)
- Checkpoint format: binary snapshot of VirtualClock state, ReplayScheduler queue, SideEffectLog, current event_position
- Checkpoint storage: alongside artifact file as .ftreplay.ckpt (overwritten each time)
- Resume: ReplayCheckpointer::resume(artifact_path) detects .ckpt file and resumes from last checkpoint
- Checkpoint is atomic: write to temp file, fsync, rename

### DeterministicFailureSemantics
- When replay encounters an error (unknown event kind, schema mismatch, corrupt event):
  - Default: halt with ReplayError and checkpoint current state
  - Lenient mode: log error, skip event, continue (with skip counter in report)
  - Strict mode: halt immediately, no checkpoint (for debugging)
- Failure mode is configurable per replay invocation
- All errors include: event_position, event_id, error_type, context

### ReplayReport
- Generated at replay completion (or failure)
- Fields: total_events, events_replayed, events_skipped, decisions_made, duration_ms, checkpoints_written, failure (if any)
- Report is deterministic: same artifact + same engine version = same report (except wall_clock_ms)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Checkpoint saves VirtualClock state correctly
- Checkpoint saves ReplayScheduler queue correctly
- Checkpoint saves current event_position
- Resume from checkpoint continues at correct position
- Resume produces same decisions as fresh replay from start
- Checkpoint is atomic (simulate crash during write, verify old checkpoint intact)
- Default mode halts on unknown event kind
- Lenient mode skips unknown event, increments skip counter
- Strict mode halts immediately without checkpoint
- ReplayReport total_events matches artifact event count
- ReplayReport is deterministic across runs (excluding wall_clock_ms)
- No checkpoint file when replay completes without error
- Checkpoint file cleaned up on successful completion

### Proptest Properties
- P-11 (from taxonomy): Checkpoint/resume equivalence — replay with checkpoint produces identical decisions as replay without
- P-12: Deterministic failure — same corrupt event always produces same error at same position

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_checkpoint.sh
- Scenario 1: Replay 50K-event artifact with checkpoint interval 10K, verify 4 checkpoints written
- Scenario 2: Kill replay at event 25K, resume from checkpoint, verify final output matches fresh replay
- Scenario 3: Inject corrupt event at position 1000, verify halt in default mode
- Scenario 4: Same corrupt event in lenient mode, verify skip and continuation
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"checkpoint","scenario":N,"checkpoints":N,"events_replayed":N,"resumed_from":N|null,"status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Large replay runs (100K+ events) take minutes; a crash at 95% means starting over. Checkpoints enable recovery.
- Measurable outcome: Resume from checkpoint completes replay in <10% of original time.
- No-regression: Checkpoint is optional; default behavior (no checkpoint file) unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Scope is fully preserved with no feature/behavior regression relative to the parent contract.
2. Comprehensive unit tests cover happy paths, boundary/edge cases, and explicit failure/error branches.
3. Deterministic integration and end-to-end scripts validate nominal, degraded, failure, and recovery scenarios.
4. Validation emits structured logs/artifacts with at least: `timestamp`, `component`, `scenario_id`, `correlation_id`, `decision_path`, `inputs`, `outcome`, `reason_code`/`error_code`, and `artifact_path`.
5. Release/promotion decisions are gated by auditable evidence bundles and explicit go/no-go criteria.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Replay can checkpoint and resume with equivalence guarantees.
2. Failure semantics are deterministic and documented.
3. Resume path preserves ordering and state invariants.
4. Recovery tests cover interruption and restart scenarios.
5. Verification requirement: includes task-scoped unit, integration, and property tests where applicable, at least one end-to-end harness script, and structured JSON logging with deterministic run_id, step, status, duration, and error context fields.
6. e2e harness requirement: at least one realistic e2e script per task path must run in CI and emit structured JSON logs with run_id, scenario_id where relevant, timing, assertions, and failure context.

title: [replay][T3.1] Define counterfactual override package format and loader
description:
Define the override package format that specifies what alternative rules/workflows/policies to swap in during counterfactual replay, and build the loader.

## Deliverables

### OverridePackage Format (.ftoverride)
- TOML-based format with sections: [meta], [[pattern_overrides]], [[workflow_overrides]], [[policy_overrides]]
- [meta]: name, description, base_artifact (path to .ftreplay), created_at, author
- [[pattern_overrides]]: rule_id, action (replace|disable|add), new_definition (inline or file ref), definition_hash (computed)
- [[workflow_overrides]]: workflow_id, action (replace|disable|add), new_steps (inline or file ref)
- [[policy_overrides]]: policy_id, action (replace|disable|add), new_rules
- Supports wildcard rule_id patterns: "rate_limit_*" overrides all rate limit rules

### OverridePackageLoader
- OverridePackageLoader::load(path) -> Result<OverridePackage> validates and parses .ftoverride
- Validates: all referenced rule_ids exist in the base artifact, no conflicting overrides
- Computes definition_hash for each override (enables diff detection)
- Returns OverrideManifest: list of (original_definition_hash, override_definition_hash) pairs

### OverrideApplicator
- Plugs into ReplayScheduler: at each decision point, checks if rule_id has an override
- If override exists: substitutes the override rule/workflow/policy definition
- Records substitution in provenance log: {"override":"applied","rule_id":"...","original_hash":"...","override_hash":"..."}

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)

- Parse .ftoverride with only pattern_overrides
- Reject .ftoverride with conflicting overrides (same rule_id, different actions)

- definition_hash computed correctly for inline definition

- OverrideApplicator substitutes correct rule at decision point
- OverrideApplicator records substitution in provenance log

- OverrideManifest lists all (original, override) hash pairs
- Empty override package is valid (no overrides, baseline replay)

title: [replay][T3.2] Implement fault-injection DSL for high-value failure modes
description:
Implement a DSL for injecting faults (delays, failures, missing events) into replay traces to test system resilience.

## Deliverables

### FaultInjectionDSL
- TOML-based fault specification embedded in .ftoverride or standalone .ftfault file
- Fault types:
  - delay(event_filter, duration_ms): inject delay before matching events
  - drop(event_filter, probability): drop matching events with given probability
  - corrupt(event_filter, field, mutation): corrupt specific field of matching events
  - reorder(event_filter, window_size): shuffle events within a window
  - duplicate(event_filter, count): duplicate matching events
- event_filter: predicate on pane_id, event_kind, time_range, sequence_range
- Deterministic: faults use seeded PRNG (seed specified in fault spec)

### FaultInjector
- FaultInjector wraps event iterator, applies fault specs to events as they flow through
- Integrates with ReplayScheduler: injector sits between ArtifactReader and scheduler
- Records all injected faults in FaultLog: {"fault_type":"delay","event_id":"...","original":"...","injected":"..."}
- FaultLog included in replay report for traceability

### High-Value Failure Modes (built-in presets)
- rate_limit_storm: inject burst of 100 events in 1ms window (tests backpressure)
- pane_death: drop all events for a pane after timestamp T (tests missing-pane handling)
- clock_skew: inject monotonicity violation (tests clock anomaly recovery)
- network_partition: delay all events by 5000ms for duration (tests timeout handling)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Parse each fault type from TOML
- delay fault injects correct duration
- drop fault drops events with correct probability (statistical test, 1000 events)
- corrupt fault modifies correct field
- reorder fault shuffles within window but not beyond
- duplicate fault creates correct number of copies
- Seeded PRNG produces deterministic faults across runs
- event_filter correctly matches pane_id, event_kind, time_range
- FaultLog records all injected faults
- Built-in preset: rate_limit_storm produces burst
- Built-in preset: pane_death drops correct pane events
- Built-in preset: clock_skew violates monotonicity
- Empty fault spec produces no modifications

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_fault_injection.sh
- Scenario 1: Inject delay on pattern-match events, verify replay handles correctly
- Scenario 2: Drop 10% of events, verify replay completes in lenient mode with skip count
- Scenario 3: Apply rate_limit_storm preset, verify backpressure response
- Scenario 4: Apply pane_death preset, verify remaining panes continue correctly
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"fault_injection","scenario":N,"faults_injected":N,"events_affected":N,"replay_completed":true|false,"status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Operators cannot test "what happens if this pane dies mid-session?" without killing it in production. Fault injection makes resilience testing safe and reproducible.
- Measurable outcome: All 4 high-value failure modes testable against any captured trace.
- No-regression: Fault injection is optional; clean replay works without it.

title: [replay][T3.4] Add simulation guardrails and fail-closed safety controls
description:
Add safety guardrails and fail-closed controls to prevent counterfactual simulations from affecting production state.

## Deliverables

### SimulationGuard
- SimulationGuard::enter() sets thread-local simulation flag
- All side-effect APIs check simulation flag before executing
- If simulation flag is set and LiveBarrier is accidentally used: panic with clear message
- SimulationGuard::exit() clears flag and validates SideEffectLog (no leaked effects)

### ResourceLimits
- Max events per replay: configurable, default 1M (prevents runaway replays)
- Max wall-clock time: configurable, default 30 minutes
- Max memory: track approximate memory via event count heuristic (no actual memory limit, but warning at threshold)
- Max concurrent replays: configurable, default 4 (prevents resource exhaustion)
- Exceeding any limit: fail-closed (halt replay, emit error, clean up)

### FailClosedSemantics
- Any unhandled error during counterfactual replay: halt, clean up, report
- No partial results: either complete result or error (no silent truncation)
- Cleanup: remove temp files, release locks, emit shutdown log
- Watchdog: if replay hangs (no progress for configurable timeout), force-terminate and report

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- SimulationGuard sets thread-local flag
- SimulationGuard panics on LiveBarrier use during simulation
- SimulationGuard clears flag on exit
- SimulationGuard validates SideEffectLog on exit
- Max events limit halts replay at correct position
- Max wall-clock time halts replay
- Max concurrent replays rejects excess
- FailClosed: unhandled error produces clean halt
- FailClosed: no partial results on error
- Cleanup removes temp checkpoint files
- Cleanup releases file locks
- Watchdog detects hung replay (mock progress stall)
- ResourceLimits configurable from TOML
- Default limits are sensible (not too restrictive, not too permissive)

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_guardrails.sh
- Scenario 1: Set max events to 100, replay 1000-event artifact, verify halt at 100
- Scenario 2: Set max time to 1s, replay slow artifact, verify timeout
- Scenario 3: Attempt to use LiveBarrier during simulation, verify panic/error
- Scenario 4: Simulate hung replay (inject infinite loop fault), verify watchdog terminates
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"guardrails","scenario":N,"limit_type":"events|time|concurrent|barrier","triggered":true,"cleanup_complete":true,"status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Counterfactual replay without guardrails could leak effects to production, exhaust resources, or hang indefinitely. This bead makes it safe to experiment.
- Measurable outcome: Zero resource leaks or production side-effects from counterfactual runs (verified by SimulationGuard + SideEffectLog).

title: [replay][T4.1] Define normalized decision graph model for replay outputs
description:
Define the normalized graph model that represents replay decision sequences for diffing and analysis.

## Deliverables

### DecisionGraph
- DecisionGraph struct: DAG of DecisionNode connected by causal edges
- DecisionNode: { node_id, decision_type, rule_id, definition_hash, input_hash, output_hash, timestamp_ms, pane_id }
- CausalEdge: { from_node, to_node, edge_type (triggered_by | preceded_by | overridden_by) }
- Build from replay output: DecisionGraph::from_decisions(decisions: &[DecisionEvent]) -> DecisionGraph

### GraphNormalization
- Canonicalize node ordering by (timestamp_ms, pane_id, rule_id) for deterministic comparison
- Remove transient fields (wall_clock_ms, replay_run_id) from comparison
- Normalize output_hash: hash only L1-equivalent fields (per equivalence contract)

### GraphOperations
- graph.nodes_by_type(DecisionType) -> iterator
- graph.causal_chain(node_id) -> Vec<DecisionNode> (ancestors)
- graph.effects(node_id) -> Vec<DecisionNode> (descendants)
- graph.roots() -> Vec<DecisionNode> (nodes with no predecessors)
- graph.to_json() -> serde_json::Value (serializable for reports)

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Build graph from empty decisions list
- Build graph from single decision
- Build graph from 100 decisions with causal links
- Causal edges link triggered_by correctly
- Canonicalization produces same node order regardless of input order
- Normalization removes wall_clock_ms from comparison
- nodes_by_type returns correct subset
- causal_chain returns full ancestor chain
- effects returns all descendants
- roots returns correct set
- to_json roundtrip preserves graph structure
- Graph with cycles detected and rejected (decisions should be DAG)

- Scenario 1: Replay artifact, build graph, verify node count matches decision count
- Scenario 2: Verify causal chains: pattern_match -> workflow_step -> policy_decision

title: [replay][T4.2] Implement baseline-vs-candidate decision diff algorithm
description:
Implement the core diff algorithm that compares baseline and candidate decision graphs to identify behavioral divergences.

## Deliverables

### DecisionDiffAlgorithm
- diff(baseline: &DecisionGraph, candidate: &DecisionGraph) -> DecisionDiff
- Matching: align decisions by (timestamp_ms, pane_id, rule_id) tuple
- Divergence types:
  - Added: decision in candidate but not baseline
  - Removed: decision in baseline but not candidate  
  - Modified: same (timestamp, pane, rule) but different output_hash
  - Shifted: same decision but different timestamp (within tolerance)
- Tolerance: configurable time tolerance for Shifted detection (default 100ms)

### DecisionDiff
- divergences: Vec<Divergence> where Divergence = { position, divergence_type, baseline_node, candidate_node, root_cause }
- root_cause: RootCause struct = { rule_id, baseline_definition_hash, candidate_definition_hash, override_applied }
- summary: DiffSummary = { total_baseline, total_candidate, unchanged, added, removed, modified, shifted }
- is_equivalent(level: EquivalenceLevel) -> bool — checks against equivalence contract

### RootCauseAttribution
- For each Modified divergence: compare definition_hashes to determine if rule changed
- If definition_hash differs: root_cause = rule_definition_change(rule_id)
- If definition_hash same but output differs: root_cause = input_divergence(upstream pane/event)
- Attribution follows causal chain upstream until it finds the first divergence point

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Diff of identical graphs produces empty divergence list
- Diff detects Added decision
- Diff detects Removed decision
- Diff detects Modified decision with correct output_hash difference
- Diff detects Shifted decision within tolerance
- Diff does NOT flag Shifted as Modified when within tolerance
- Root cause attribution: rule definition change
- Root cause attribution: input divergence (upstream)
- Root cause attribution: override applied
- is_equivalent(L1) returns true when only timing differs
- is_equivalent(L0) returns true when event structure matches
- DiffSummary counts are correct
- Large diff (1000 divergences) completes in <1s

### Proptest Properties
- P-16 (from taxonomy): diff(A, A) = empty divergences for any valid graph A
- P-17: diff(A, B) divergences are inverse of diff(B, A) (added/removed swap)
- P-18: root_cause attribution always points to a real node in baseline or candidate

### E2E Test Script: tests/e2e/test_replay_decision_diff.sh
- Scenario 1: Replay same artifact twice (no overrides), verify zero divergences
- Scenario 2: Replay with one rule override, verify exactly the expected divergences
- Scenario 3: Replay with multiple overrides, verify root causes correctly attributed
- Scenario 4: Diff with shifted timing (clock jitter), verify tolerance handling
- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"decision_diff","scenario":N,"divergences":N,"added":N,"removed":N,"modified":N,"root_causes_attributed":N,"status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Manual comparison of decision sequences is error-prone and slow. Automated diff with root-cause attribution turns hours of investigation into seconds.
- Measurable outcome: Every divergence includes machine-readable root cause within 1s of diff computation.

title: [replay][T4.3] Build severity taxonomy and risk scoring for drift
description:
Build severity taxonomy and risk scoring to classify divergences by impact: cosmetic vs behavioral vs safety-critical.

## Deliverables

### DivergenceSeverity
- Severity levels: Info, Low, Medium, High, Critical
- Classification rules:
  - Info: timing shift only (Shifted divergence within tolerance)
  - Low: added/removed detection with confidence < 0.5
  - Medium: modified detection output (different matched_text or severity)
  - High: modified workflow decision (different StepResult)
  - Critical: modified policy decision (Allow changed to Deny or vice versa)

### RiskScorer
- RiskScorer::score(divergence: &Divergence) -> RiskScore
- RiskScore: { severity, impact_radius (number of downstream decisions affected), confidence, explanation }
- impact_radius: count of nodes in DecisionGraph reachable from divergence point
- Aggregate risk: RiskScorer::aggregate(divergences: &[Divergence]) -> AggregateRisk
- AggregateRisk: { max_severity, total_risk_score, critical_count, high_count, recommendation }
- recommendation: Pass | Review | Block based on aggregate thresholds

### SeverityConfiguration
- Configurable severity rules via severity_rules.toml
- Custom rules: map (decision_type, rule_id_pattern) -> severity_override
- Example: all rate_limit_* policy changes are Critical regardless of default

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Shifted divergence classified as Info
- Low-confidence detection classified as Low
- Modified detection classified as Medium
- Modified workflow step classified as High
- Policy Allow->Deny classified as Critical
- impact_radius correctly counts downstream nodes
- Aggregate risk max_severity is highest individual severity
- Aggregate risk recommendation: Pass when all Info/Low
- Aggregate risk recommendation: Block when any Critical
- Custom severity override applies correctly
- Default severity used when no custom rule matches
- Empty divergences produce Pass recommendation
- Severity ordering: Info < Low < Medium < High < Critical

- Scenario 2: Diff with policy change, verify recommendation = Block

- Structured JSON logging: {"test":"risk_scoring","scenario":N,"divergences":N,"max_severity":"Info|Low|Medium|High|Critical","recommendation":"Pass|Review|Block","status":"pass|fail"}

## User Impact
- Pain removed: Not all divergences are equal. Without severity scoring, operators must manually assess each divergence. Risk scoring automates triage.

description:

## Command Syntax
- `ft replay capture [--output PATH] [--pane-filter IDs] [--duration SECS]` — Start capture, write .ftreplay artifact

title: [replay][T5.4] Implement replay artifact registry UX (list/inspect/retention/prune)
description:
Implement replay artifact registry UX for listing, inspecting, managing retention, and pruning artifacts.

## Deliverables

### ArtifactRegistry
- ArtifactRegistry struct backed by manifest.toml in tests/regression/replay/
- Operations: list, inspect, add, retire, prune
- list: returns all artifacts with metadata (name, size, event_count, created_at, sensitivity_tier, status)
- inspect: returns detailed artifact info (header, entity count, decision count, checksums)
- add: registers new artifact, updates manifest, validates integrity
- retire: marks artifact as retired with reason (not deleted, just excluded from regression suite)
- prune: removes retired artifacts older than retention period

### CLI Commands (via ft replay artifact subcommand)
- ft replay artifact list [--format json|table] [--tier T1|T2|T3]
- ft replay artifact inspect <path>
- ft replay artifact add <path> [--label <label>]
- ft replay artifact retire <path> --reason <reason>
- ft replay artifact prune [--dry-run] [--max-age-days N]

### Manifest Format (manifest.toml)
- [[artifacts]]: path, label, sha256, event_count, decision_count, created_at, sensitivity_tier, status (active|retired)
- Manifest is append-only log (per charter principle 5.6)
- Manifest validation: all referenced paths exist, all checksums match

title: [replay][T6.2] Add determinism and semantic-equivalence property test suite
description:

## Deliverables

### Replay Determinism Properties
- tests/proptest_replay_determinism.rs:

title: [replay][T6.3] Define and enforce performance budgets for capture/replay/diff pipeline
description:
Define and enforce performance budgets for the capture/replay/diff pipeline to prevent regressions in speed.

## Deliverables

### PerformanceBudgets
- Capture budget: <1ms per event overhead (measured as capture_time / event_count)
- Replay budget: >=100K events/sec in instant mode
- Diff budget: <1s for 1000 divergences
- Report generation: <100ms for standard report
- Artifact read: >=500K events/sec streaming rate

### BenchmarkSuite
- benches/replay_capture.rs: Criterion benchmark for capture adapter overhead
- benches/replay_kernel.rs: Criterion benchmark for replay throughput
- benches/replay_diff.rs: Criterion benchmark for diff algorithm
- Baseline: record initial measurements, detect regressions >10%

### BudgetEnforcer
- CI integration: run benchmarks on every PR, compare against baselines
- Warning: >10% regression in any metric
- Blocking: >25% regression in any metric
- Baseline update: automatic after merge to main

## Test Requirements

### Unit Tests (>=30)
- Capture overhead measurement is accurate (mock timer)
- Replay throughput measurement is accurate
- Budget comparison correctly identifies regression
- Budget comparison correctly identifies improvement

4. Run regression suite → verify pass/fail gate behavior
5. Inspect and export artifacts → verify human-readable output
6. Robot Mode: agent issues replay commands → verify structured responses

## Pilot Participants
- At least 2 human operators (running ft CLI manually)
- At least 2 agent workflows (using Robot Mode or MCP)

## Success Metrics
- Time-to-first-success: each workflow completes within 5 minutes on first attempt
- Error rate: <10% of operations produce unexpected errors
- Confusion rate: <20% of operations require documentation lookup

## Deliverables
- Pilot script with step-by-step instructions for each scenario
- Structured feedback log capturing friction points, errors, confusion patterns
- Prioritized improvements list filed as new beads or bead amendments
- Summary report documenting time-to-first-success, error rates, and top 5 improvement recommendations
- No unit tests required (operational activity, not code implementation)

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Deliver full scope for this bead without regressions in adjacent behavior.
2. Add comprehensive unit tests for happy path, boundary/edge behavior, and explicit failure/error handling.
3. Add deterministic integration/end-to-end scenarios including at least one failure injection and one recovery path.
4. Emit detailed structured logs (timestamp, component, correlation_id, scenario_id, inputs, decisions, outcomes, reason_code/error_code) and persist triage artifacts.
5. Document run commands and evidence locations and wire them into normal validation/CI paths.

## User Impact
1. Specify the concrete operator/agent workflow pain this bead removes (speed, reliability, safety, or clarity).
2. Define measurable user-facing outcomes (for example p95 latency, failure/timeout rate, time-to-recovery, or reduction in manual intervention steps).
3. Define no-regression UX guarantees and explicit rollback/degradation behavior if those outcomes are not met.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Pilot covers representative human and agent workflows with explicit success metrics and baseline comparisons.
2. Results include friction taxonomy, severity ranking, and prioritized remediation backlog linked to bead IDs.
3. Gate policy updates are proposed where usability risks affect safe adoption or incident response speed.
4. Unit and integration tests are added for high-frequency UX failure paths discovered in pilot.
5. At least one realistic e2e script reproduces top pilot failure mode and verifies the fix path in CI.
6. Structured JSON logs include participant_type, workflow_id, step, failure_mode, remediation_outcome, and run metadata.
7. Exit criteria: pilot demonstrates measurable improvement in completion rate, error recovery time, and operator confidence, otherwise rollout remains blocked.
notes: This preserves technical rigor while ensuring the system is compelling and practical for real users.

description:
# [EPIC] Interactive Tutorial: wa learn

## Mission
Provide an in-terminal interactive tutorial system that guides new users through wa's capabilities, builds confidence, and dramatically reduces time-to-first-success.

## Why This Matters
Terminal automation tools are intimidating. Users face a steep learning curve:
- "Where do I start?"
- "What can this tool actually do?"
- "How do I know if I set it up correctly?"

An interactive tutorial transforms this experience:
- **Guided**: Step-by-step progression with clear goals
- **Safe**: Sandbox/simulation mode prevents accidents
- **Immediate**: Users see results within minutes
- **Contextual**: Tutorial adapts to user's environment

## Core Insight: Learning by Doing
Reading docs is passive. `wa learn` provides active learning:
1. User runs `wa learn`
2. Tutorial detects their environment (WezTerm running? Agents present?)
3. Presents contextual exercises with immediate feedback
4. Tracks progress across sessions

## Scope

### Core Tutorial Tracks
- **Track 1: Basics** (5 min) - What is wa? Start watching. View status.
- **Track 2: Events** (10 min) - Understanding detections. Pattern matching.
- **Track 3: Workflows** (15 min) - Automating responses. Policy gates.
- **Track 4: Robot Mode** (10 min) - Building agent integrations.
- **Track 5: Advanced** (20 min) - Custom patterns. Multi-agent coordination.

### Features
- Progress persistence (resume where left off)
- Environment detection (skip irrelevant steps)
- Sandbox mode (no real actions, simulated feedback)
- Achievement system (motivates completion)
- Help escape hatch (`wa learn --help-me` for contextual guidance)

## Success Criteria
- New user can complete Track 1 in <5 minutes
- 80% of users who start Track 1 complete Track 2
- Time-to-first-success decreases by 50%
- Support burden decreases (users self-serve)

## Testing Requirements
- Unit tests for tutorial state machine
- Integration tests for environment detection
- E2E tests for full track completion
- Golden output tests for tutorial text
- User testing with 3+ developers unfamiliar with wa

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `wa learn` command launches interactive tutorial
- [ ] 5 tracks implemented with 3-10 exercises each
- [ ] Progress persisted in ~/.config/wa/learn.json
- [ ] Sandbox mode prevents real actions
- [ ] Environment detection guides appropriate exercises
- [ ] Help escape (`wa learn --help-me`) provides context
- [ ] Tests cover all tracks and state transitions

title: Environment detection: detect WezTerm, agents, config state for contextual exercises
description:
# Environment detection for tutorial

## Purpose
Detect the user's environment to provide contextual exercises and skip irrelevant steps. A user without WezTerm running shouldn't do "start watching" exercises.

## Background
Different users have different setups:
- WezTerm running vs not
- Agents present vs empty panes
- wa configured vs fresh install
- Existing DB vs first time

The tutorial should adapt to each situation.

## Implementation Details

### Environment Checks
```rust
pub struct TutorialEnvironment {
    wezterm_running: bool,
    wezterm_version: Option<String>,
    pane_count: usize,
    agent_panes: Vec<AgentInfo>, // Panes with detected agents
    wa_configured: bool,         // wa.toml exists
    db_has_data: bool,           // Segments/events exist
    shell_integration: bool,     // OSC 133 markers detected
}

impl TutorialEnvironment {
    pub async fn detect() -> Self { ... }
    
    pub fn can_run_exercise(&self, exercise: &Exercise) -> CanRun {
        match exercise.requirements {
            Requires::WeztermRunning if !self.wezterm_running => 
                CanRun::No("Start WezTerm first"),
            Requires::AgentPresent if self.agent_panes.is_empty() => 
                CanRun::Simulation("No agents detected, using simulation"),
            _ => CanRun::Yes,
        }
    }
}
```

### Exercise Requirements
Each exercise declares its requirements:
```rust
pub struct Exercise {
    id: ExerciseId,
    title: String,
    requirements: Vec<Requirement>,
    can_simulate: bool,  // True if exercise works in sandbox mode
}
```

### Adaptive Flow
1. User starts track
2. Detect environment
3. For each exercise:
   - Check requirements
   - If met: run exercise
   - If not met but can_simulate: run in sandbox
   - If not met and can't simulate: skip with explanation

## Testing
- Unit tests for each detection check
- Mock tests for different environment states
- Integration tests with real WezTerm (optional, CI skip)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TutorialEnvironment struct with all detection fields
- [ ] detect() function checks all conditions
- [ ] can_run_exercise() returns appropriate guidance
- [ ] Clear user messaging for skipped exercises
- [ ] Tests for all detection paths

title: Sandbox mode: simulated WezTerm and safe execution for tutorial
description:
# Sandbox mode for tutorial

## Purpose
Provide a safe, simulated environment where tutorial exercises run without affecting real panes or executing dangerous commands.

## Relationship to Simulation Mode (wa-a0c)
**IMPORTANT**: This task builds on the simulation infrastructure from wa-a0c.

The tutorial sandbox is a **pre-configured simulation scenario** that:
1. Uses `MockWezterm` from wa-a0c for pane simulation
2. Uses the scenario system from wa-a0c.3 for mock data
3. Adds tutorial-specific features (visual indicators, command hints)

This is NOT a separate mock implementation - it reuses and extends wa-a0c.

## Background
Users may:
- Not have WezTerm running
- Not have agents in their panes
- Be afraid to let tutorial "do things"

Sandbox mode addresses all these concerns by using simulation.

## Implementation Details

### Sandbox as Simulation Wrapper
```rust
pub struct TutorialSandbox {
    /// Reuses simulation infrastructure from wa-a0c
    simulation: MockWezterm,
    
    /// Tutorial-specific state
    current_exercise: Option<ExerciseId>,
    hints_shown: Vec<HintId>,
    command_log: Vec<SandboxCommand>,
}

impl TutorialSandbox {
    pub fn new() -> Self {
        // Load tutorial-specific scenario
        let scenario = Scenario::load_builtin("tutorial/sandbox.yaml").unwrap();
        let mut simulation = MockWezterm::new();
        scenario.apply_to(&simulation).unwrap();
        
        Self {
            simulation,
            current_exercise: None,
            hints_shown: vec\![],
            command_log: vec\![],
        }
    }
}
```

### Tutorial Sandbox Scenario
```yaml
# scenarios/tutorial/sandbox.yaml
name: tutorial_sandbox
description: "Pre-configured environment for wa learn exercises"

panes:
  - id: 0
    title: "Local Shell"
    domain: "local"
    cwd: "/home/user/projects"
    
  - id: 1
    title: "Codex Agent"
    domain: "local"
    agent_type: codex
    initial_content: |
      codex> Ready to help with your project.
      What would you like to work on?

  - id: 2
    title: "Claude Code"
    domain: "local"
    agent_type: claude_code
    initial_content: |
      claude> Analyzing your codebase...

# Inject events based on exercise triggers
exercise_events:
  track1_ex2:  # When user reaches this exercise
    - at: 0s
      pane: 1
      action: append
      content: |
        [Usage Warning]
        Approaching daily usage limit.
```

### Visual Indicators
- `[SANDBOX]` prefix on all output
- Distinct colors for simulated vs real
- Clear "exit sandbox" instructions
- Hint tooltips for tutorial context

### Command Logging
```rust
impl TutorialSandbox {
    pub fn execute(&mut self, cmd: &WaCommand) -> Result<String> {
        // Log for tutorial feedback
        self.command_log.push(SandboxCommand {
            command: cmd.clone(),
            timestamp: Utc::now(),
            exercise: self.current_exercise.clone(),
        });
        
        // Execute against mock
        let result = self.simulation.execute(cmd).await?;
        
        // Wrap with sandbox indicator
        Ok(format\!("[SANDBOX] {}", result))
    }
}
```

## Testing
- Unit tests verify sandbox uses simulation correctly
- Tests for tutorial-specific features (hints, logging)
- E2E tests for full sandbox flow in tutorial context

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Sandbox uses MockWezterm from wa-a0c
- [ ] Tutorial scenario provides realistic mock data
- [ ] Visual indicators clearly show sandbox mode
- [ ] Command logging tracks tutorial progress
- [ ] Exercise-triggered events work
- [ ] Tests verify integration with simulation

title: Shell integration installer: enable OSC 133 prompt markers (bash/zsh/fish)
description:
# Task: Shell integration installer (OSC 133 markers)

## Goal
Provide a guided, idempotent way to enable OSC 133 prompt markers so wa can detect:
- prompt boundaries
- command start/end
- "pane is idle/ready" reliably

## Why
We want to avoid brittle heuristics that guess prompts based on `❯`/`$`.
OSC 133 is the robust path.

## Minimal marker emission (PLAN §4.6; illustrative)
The installer should ultimately produce equivalent semantics to:

```bash
# ~/.config/wa/shell-integration.bash (sourced by user's .bashrc)
__wa_prompt_start() { printf '\e]133;A\a'; }
__wa_command_start() { printf '\e]133;C\a'; }
__wa_command_end() { printf '\e]133;D;%s\a' "$?"; }
PROMPT_COMMAND='__wa_prompt_start'
trap '__wa_command_end' DEBUG  # Simplified; real impl must be more robust
```

Notes:
- This snippet is intentionally simplified in the plan; the real implementation must avoid breaking shells.
- The key requirement is emitting the correct OSC 133 sequences so wa can deterministically infer PromptActive/CommandRunning and exit codes.

## Approach
- `wa setup --shell` detects current shell (and can accept `--shell bash|zsh|fish`).
- Install minimal shell snippets into appropriate rc files:
  - `~/.bashrc`, `~/.zshrc`, `~/.config/fish/config.fish`
- Changes are idempotent and include a clear managed marker block.
- Always create a backup copy before modifying.

## Deliverables
- Shell snippet templates.
- Detection and idempotent patching logic.

## Testing
- Unit/fixture tests (see `wa-nu4.3.3.5`):
  - inserts exactly one managed block
  - re-running is a no-op
  - backups are created
- E2E:

- After setup, a sample interactive session emits OSC 133 markers.

title: Layout tree capture — window/tab/pane hierarchy with split topology
description:
## Goal
Capture the complete window -> tab -> pane layout hierarchy including split topology (horizontal/vertical splits with ratios) from the running mux server.

## Background
WezTerm organizes panes in a tree structure: Windows contain Tabs, Tabs contain a tree of Panes split horizontally or vertically. The resurrect.wezterm plugin captures this via Lua, but we need to capture it programmatically via the mux protocol or CLI.

The wezterm cli list command provides flat pane info (pane_id, tab_id, window_id, workspace, title, cwd, size). But it does NOT provide split topology information. To capture the full tree, we need either:
a) The vendored mux client with appropriate PDUs
b) A Lua script executed via wezterm cli (wezterm lua)
c) Parsing from wezterm cli list-clients or other commands

## Design
1. Primary approach: Use wezterm's Lua API via `wezterm cli spawn --` or custom Lua:
   ```lua
   -- Enumerate full layout tree
   for _, window in ipairs(wezterm.mux.all_windows()) do
     for _, tab in ipairs(window:tabs()) do
       local panes_with_info = tab:panes_with_info()
       -- panes_with_info includes: pane, is_active, left, top, width, height, pixel_width, pixel_height, index
     end
   end
   ```

2. Fallback: Parse flat pane list + infer splits from position/size data
   - wezterm cli list provides pane dimensions (left, top, width, height)
   - Can reconstruct the split tree from spatial relationships
   - Less reliable but doesn't require Lua execution

3. Capture workspace assignments for each window
4. Capture active tab per window, active pane per tab
5. Build the recursive PaneNode tree from the layout data

## Key Consideration
The panes_with_info() Lua method returns positional data that can be used to reconstruct the split tree. Each pane has left/top/width/height in cells. Adjacent panes sharing an edge at the same position indicate a split boundary.

## Algorithm for tree reconstruction from flat position data:
1. Start with all panes in a tab
2. Find the split axis (vertical or horizontal) by checking if panes can be partitioned into two groups along x or y axis
3. Recursively build subtrees for each partition
4. Compute split ratio from the size proportions

## Dependencies
- Requires MuxSnapshot schema (bead 1) for WindowSnapshot, TabSnapshot, PaneNode

## Acceptance Criteria
- Correctly captures split topology for: single pane, 2-way split, 3-way split, nested splits
- Captures active tab/pane state
- Handles workspaces
- Works via both Lua approach and fallback position-inference approach
- Roundtrip test: capture layout, serialize, deserialize, verify matches original

## Benchmark & Property Testing Requirements

### Proptest
Add `tests/proptest_layout_tree.rs`:
- **tree_serialization_roundtrip**: For any arbitrary PaneNode tree (proptest generates random trees with 1-20 leaves, random HSplit/VSplit nesting, random ratios 0.1-0.9), assert that serde_json::from_str(serde_json::to_string(tree)) == tree. This validates that no layout topology is lost during serialization.
- **tree_from_positions_roundtrip**: For any valid PaneNode tree, compute the flat position list (left, top, width, height for each leaf), then reconstruct the tree from positions. Assert the reconstructed tree is structurally equivalent to the original.
- **split_ratio_preservation**: For any tree with arbitrary split ratios, assert that ratios survive roundtrip within f64 epsilon tolerance.

### Criterion Benchmarks
Add `benches/layout_tree.rs` using criterion:
- **tree_traversal_depth**: Benchmark traversal (collect all leaf PaneSnapshots) for trees of depth 2, 4, 8, 16. Target: <10us for depth 8 (typical max nesting).
- **tree_reconstruction_from_positions**: Benchmark the algorithm that reconstructs PaneNode tree from flat pane position data, for 2, 5, 10, 20 panes.
- **tree_serialization**: Benchmark serde_json serialization/deserialization for trees with 5, 20, 50 leaf panes.

## Cross-References
- **wa-e6pq** (Layout restoration engine): wa-ooje captures the layout tree; wa-e6pq consumes it to recreate the physical window/tab/split topology. The PaneNode tree structure defined here is the contract between capture and restore. Any changes to the tree representation must be coordinated between both beads.
- **wa-2dd4s.3** (Swap layouts): FrankenTerm's swap-layout feature allows users to switch between saved layout configurations. wa-ooje's layout tree capture provides the serialized format that swap-layouts will store and retrieve. Ensure the PaneNode schema supports metadata fields (e.g., layout name, tags) needed by the swap-layout system.
close_reason: Implemented: session_topology.rs with TopologySnapshot::from_panes(), infer_split_tree(), PaneNode recursive tree (HSplit/VSplit/Leaf), match_panes() for restore, 14 passing tests.

title: Replace Mutex::lock().unwrap() poison handling
description:
# Background
UBS flagged 13 instances of `Mutex::lock().unwrap()` or `.expect()`, notably in `replay_capture.rs`.

# Justification
If a thread panics while holding a standard library Mutex, the mutex is "poisoned". Subsequent threads calling `.unwrap()` on the lock result will also panic, causing a cascading failure that takes down the process.

# Implementation Notes
- Replace `.unwrap()` with `match lock.lock() { Ok(g) => g, Err(poisoned) => poisoned.into_inner() }` to recover the guard, OR return a designated error if the subsystem cannot safely continue with potentially corrupted state.

title: E2E script: watch-and-notify mode (--notify-only events → notifications)
description:
# E2E script: watch-and-notify mode (`wa watch --notify-only`)

## Goal
Validate end-to-end that notify-only mode:
- detects events and emits notifications
- **does not auto-handle** (no workflows run, events remain unhandled)
- respects notify filters and throttling
- includes suggested actions in notifications

This is the integration proof for notify-only mode (`wa-spi`) + notifications (`wa-psm`) under the standard E2E harness.

## Key constraints
- Deterministic: **no fixed `sleep N`**. Use bounded waits (polling with timeouts) and a quiescence detector.
- Safe shutdown: watcher processes must be stopped gracefully and reliably (SIGINT/`wa stop`), with bounded waits.
- No global config mutation: use an isolated E2E workspace/config.
- Artifacts must be redacted (no transcript leakage).

## Test setup
- Start a harness-owned mock webhook server with:
  - `/received` to read captured notifications as JSON
  - `/attempt_count` (optional)
  - request logging to artifacts
- Start WezTerm mux + dummy panes that can deterministically emit known events.
- Start `wa watch` in notify-only mode in a dedicated E2E workspace:
  - `wa watch --notify-only …`
  - notifications configured to point to the mock server

## Scenarios

### 1) Notify-only mode does not auto-handle
- Start watcher: `wa watch --notify-only --workspace <e2e> …`
- Trigger a known event that would normally be auto-handled (e.g., compaction):
  - via dummy pane output (preferred) OR a harness `wa e2e emit` helper
- Wait until mock server has ≥1 received payload (poll with timeout).
- Assertions:
  - notification payload exists and references the correct `rule_id` / pane
  - `wa events --unhandled --format json` still lists the event (still unhandled)
  - `wa workflow executions` (or DB evidence) shows **no** workflow ran for that event

### 2) Notification filter
- Start watcher with a filter:
  - `wa watch --notify-only --notify-filter "usage_limit" …`
- Trigger two events:
  - one matching filter (usage limit)
  - one non-matching (compaction)
- Wait for quiescence (bounded).
- Assert mock server received exactly one notification, for the matching event.

### 3) Throttling in notify-only mode
- Configure a low throttle budget in the E2E config.
- Trigger a burst of N events quickly (deterministic dummy output).
- Wait for quiescence (bounded).
- Assert:
  - delivered notifications ≤ configured budget
  - watcher logs contain explicit “throttled” markers for skipped notifications

### 4) Suggested action included
- Trigger compaction.
- Wait for first notification.
- Assert the notification body includes a suggested remediation (e.g., `wa workflow run handle_compaction --pane <id>`).

## Registry
- Register this case in the E2E case registry (`wa-4vx.10.20`) with prerequisites and default inclusion status.

## Artifacts
- `wa_watch_notify_only.log`
- `notifications_received.json` (redacted)
- `events_unhandled.json`
- `workflow_executions_slice.json` (or other “no workflow ran” evidence)
- `mock_server.log`

## Logging contract
Every step logs:
- case/scenario name
- watcher PID/workspace
- mock server bind address
- timeouts used

Example:
```
[NOTIFYONLY_E2E] watcher started workspace=e2e pid=12345 notify_only=true filter=usage_limit
[NOTIFYONLY_E2E] emit rule_id=codex.usage_limit_reached pane=3
[NOTIFYONLY_E2E] wait received>=1 timeout=10s
[NOTIFYONLY_E2E] assert event still unhandled: OK
```

## Testing
- Determinism:
  - no fixed sleeps
  - all waits are “wait until condition” with explicit timeouts
- Correctness:
  - notification exists and matches expected `rule_id` + `pane_id`
  - event remains unhandled (no workflow execution)
  - filter and throttling behave as configured
- Shutdown reliability:
  - stop watcher via `wa stop --workspace <e2e>` when available, otherwise SIGINT + bounded wait
  - artifacts always include watcher exit status and last log lines

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Notify-only mode delivers notifications for detected events.
- [ ] Notify-only mode does not auto-handle (events remain unhandled, no workflows executed).
- [ ] Filters and throttling work deterministically.
- [ ] Notifications include suggested actions.
- [ ] Artifacts/logs are sufficient to debug failures.
